must_fix: CLARITY (must fix): b10 to b11, what causes the ending. As written, Nandini says l25 'भैयाजी को पता था।' out loud at the stall while the call is open. The next sound is Bhaiyaji's hand rustling the pocket (head of b11), and then l26 'और ये जेब में phone किसका है?'. Viewers will read that as 'her voice gave him away', the most familiar beat in any wire scene. That would make the B cliffhanger the lead's own mistake, and no later episode supports that. The writer means the opposite (writer_notes: the call is muted at her end from b7). But the mute exists only in the b7 action text. A handset lying on wool cannot show it, and no line says it. FIX: move the existing 1.0 s cloth rustle from the head of b11 to between l24 and l25, so his hand is already on the phone before she speaks. This adds no line and touches no lock, glimpse, seam or balance line. (1) b10: silent_seconds 1.5 -> 2.5. Shot 2 becomes '(insert, under the second half of l24 and the rustle after it): Pushpa's needles stopped dead in the wool beside the handset.' After l24 add: 'then 1.0 s silent: a loud rustle of cloth against the microphone through the handset, his hand finding the pocket, fully settled before l25.' (2) b11: silent_seconds 3.5 -> 2.5. Shot 1 becomes '(insert, close): the orange handset on the wool; Bhaiyaji right on top of the phone: l26.' Delete the rustle clause. The last sentence becomes 'Silence in b11 is 2.5 s in all.' (3) sfx_notes b10: append 'After l24, a loud cloth rustle against the microphone (his hand finding the pocket), 1.0 s, through the filter, settled before l25; the bed ducks under l25.' sfx_notes b11: replace its first sentence with 'l26 through the filter, close and dry, with no effect under it or just before it.' (4) writer_notes 'Format': b10 becomes '1.5 s before l24 and 1.0 s between l24 and l25'; b11 becomes '1.0 s between l26 and l27 and 1.5 s after l27'. writer_notes 'Recording logic': replace 'and shown by the handset lying on the wool' with 'and the search is heard starting before l25, so nothing said at the stall reads as the cause'. Total silence stays 22.1 s and target_total_seconds stays 124.5. S5 mirrors the same silent_seconds, action and sfx changes in script.en.json (120.1 unchanged). Any equivalent that makes the search start before l25 also works. This fix also removes the second problem in b11: l26 sitting only 0.3 s after a loud effect under a phone filter (bible writer note: 'A phone-filtered line never sits directly on a loud effect').

must_fix: CONTINUITY (must fix): Bhaiyaji's line l24 is the one s2b03 quotes word for word as the recorded evidence (D-006 change 11), but the two English files word it differently. s2b01 en l24 reads 'Fake Inspector! Aaiye... it's you I was waiting for.' s2b03 en l12 reads: In Bhaiyaji's voice: 'Fake Inspector! You are just the man I was waiting for.' Subtitles and audio would then 'quote' words the viewer never heard. s2b03 en's own writer_notes say s2b01 must use the same words or the quote must change, and s2b01's writer_notes miss this. PREFERRED FIX (s2b01 stays as it is): change s2b03 en l12 to "[quietly] In Bhaiyaji's voice: 'Fake Inspector! It's you I was waiting for.'", target 5.0 down to about 4.4 s, and change the same quote where grep finds it in <repo>/content/series2/episodes/s2b03/script.en.json (lines 165, 366, 370). Why this way round: 'it's you' keeps the stress of the Hindi 'आप ही का', which tells the viewer Bhaiyaji expected this impostor (the reason for l25 'Bhaiyaji knew.'). 'Just the man' can sound like luck. It also adds nothing to s2b01, which is already at the 1,050 measure. FALLBACK if s2b03 is locked: change s2b01 en l24 to "[laughs] Fake Inspector! Aaiye... you are just the man I was waiting for.", target 5.0 up to 5.8 s (12 more characters, so about 1,060 in all, just over the measure).
